newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM confident export growth target achievable.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM confident export growth target achievable.

text.p: Thailand's Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Sunday that he was confident the country's export growth target of 10 percent would be achieved this year.

"The April figure shows signs of recovery. We believe that our exports this year will still meet the target of 10 percent," he told reporters after a summit with key Thai exporters in this resort city.
Thai exports growth has been in the doldrums since last year. In 1996, Thai exports contracted 0.2 percent compared with 23.6 percent growth in 1995.
The commerce ministry has set an export growth target of 10 percent for this year while the central bank has set a target of 7.7 percent.

"We will support exports with good potential such as foods, automobiles and parts, computers and electronics. To cut costs for exporters the government will speed up measures such as tax incentives, reduced costs of funds and infrastructure costs," the prime minister said.
Earlier, the prermier met at a summit with key exporters who blamed the government and some of its inefficiencies for Thailand's recent dismal exports performance.

Exporters had cited the authorities's failure to cut high interest rates, red tape, corruption at the customs department and a lack of focused export strategy for the sharp slowdown in Thai exports since last year.

Thailand's economic woes have been further compounded by weak exports, slowing economic growth, offshore speculative attacks on the Thai baht, a plunging stock market and ailing finance and property sectors.
